name: Idiopathic Giant Cell Myocarditis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Giant Cell Myocarditis

criteria.description: Presence of multinucleated giant cells with extensive myocardial necrosis on endomyocardial biopsy
Rapidly progressive heart failure symptoms with arrhythmias and cardiogenic shock
Exclusion of infectious myocarditis and sarcoidosis by clinical, imaging, and laboratory evaluation
Cardiac MRI showing myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement consistent with active myocarditis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of giant cells with myocardial necrosis plus compatible clinical presentation and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Endomyocardial biopsy is the gold standard for diagnosis; early diagnosis is critical due to rapid progression.

searchTerms: passing out due to heart rhythm issues

occasional.symptomName: Palpable hepatomegaly secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure
liver enlargement due to heart disease

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to embolic events
searchTerms: brain issues caused by embolic events

rare.symptomName: Autoimmune phenomena such as rash or arthritis

imaging: Cardiac MRI showing myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement
Echocardiogram demonstrating reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and wall motion abnormalities
genetic: No known genetic mutations definitively linked; idiopathic etiology
other: Endomyocardial biopsy revealing multinucleated giant cells with myocardial necrosis
Electrocardiogram showing ventricular arrhythmias and conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Noncaseating granulomas on biopsy instead of giant cells
More chronic course with systemic sarcoidosis features
Different pattern of late gadolinium enhancement on MRI
Presence of viral genome in myocardium
Lymphocytic rather than giant cell infiltration on biopsy

redFlags: Failure to respond to standard heart failure therapies
